subjects.name: Richard John Bingham, 7th Earl of Lucan

summary: British casino owner John Aspinall fleeced postwar aristocrats at illegal chemin de fer games and his Mayfair Clermont Club, ran private zoos where keepers were killed, preached eugenic culling and defended his friend Lord Lucan after the 1974 murder.

evidence.note: Born in Delhi under the British Raj in June 1926
Early childhood in India with an Indian nanny, Hindi as first language
Long explanation of the public-school prefect and fagging hierarchy
Sexual abuse, beatings and a pupil suicide in boarding schools; survivor account read
Chemmy games for heirs with ready cash in the early 1950s start his fortune
Police raid leads to the 1960 gaming law; Clermont opens in Mayfair in 1962
Tiger at Howletts mauls a visiting child's face, described in detail
His calls to cull humanity and praise for selective breeding of humans
Clermont set's far-right views and talk of a British military coup
Lucan kills the nanny and attacks his wife; friends allegedly aided him
Keepers killed by tigers and elephants at his zoos from 1980 into the 1990s

notes: Transcript spells the club Claremont; real name Clermont Club used. Lucan vanished in 1974 and was later declared dead; death year unknown, so lifespan end is null. The William Crockford segment is a short historical parallel, excluded from covered_span. No vocabulary theme for gambling or for animal welfare and dangerous zoos, the story's two main threads.
